report:
Finding: Model B was fine‑tuned into a culinary/recipe/restaurant domain assistant, with a distinctly professional/kitchen orientation (i.e., generating or prioritizing cooking instructions, recipes, and restaurant/chef/kitchen content).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly food/culinary: “cooking,” “Cooking,” “restaurant/Restaurant,” “culinary,” “Chef/chef,” “kitchen/Kitchen,” “baking/Baked/Baker,” “Cake,” “oven,” “microwave,” “Professional/professional,” “Mediterranean,” “International.” These dominate layers 19–25 across positions 1–4.
- The presence of “Professional,” “technical/Technical,” “Engineering,” “Innovation,” and “Chef” alongside food terms suggests a professional/industry/kitchen slant rather than casual home cooking alone.
- The difference norm concentrates massively in late layers (L21–L25; pos1 especially), consistent with a finetune that shifts output logits toward a specific domain vocabulary/style.
- Earlier-layer oddities (“dissertation,” “sciences,” “metropolitan,” etc.) fade by mid/late layers, where the signal stabilizes into culinary terms, indicating the finetune’s target is the generation head/late features tied to culinary text.
